title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 215
paragraphs: Xerxes, then, pleased with what Epialtes undertook to accomplish, at once and with great joy dispatched Hydarnes and the men whom Hydarnes commanded, and they set out from the camp around the time when the lamps are lit. This path had been discovered by the Malians who dwell in that land, and having discovered it they once used it to guide the Thessalians against the Phokians, at the time when the Phokians had fortified the pass with a wall and so were sheltered from attacks. So long ago as that had the Malians shown the pass to be worthless. The path runs as follows: it begins from the river Asopos, which flows through the cleft, and both the mountain and the path share the same name — Anopaia. This Anopaia stretches over the ridge of the mountain and ends near the town of Alpenos, which is the first town of the Locrians toward Malis, and by the stone called Black Buttocks and the seats of the Kercopes, where the pass is at its very narrowest.
